# Cully 0.25.0

- **Two clear terminal sections.** Keep Harness on the left and combine native instruments and observed Cully activity under Session on the right. Quota, input/output tokens, Fast mode and Git changes stay together. The layout preserves the current health bar, hidden-duplicate behavior, agent-specific historical measurements and MCP connection checks, and stacks the same two sections on narrow terminals.
- **Discover current coding-agent techniques.** The advisor periodically researches recent releases, model updates, articles, workflows, skills, hooks and integrations using the active Claude Code, Codex or Cursor web tools. Dated public findings are filtered against the accepted task and observed session signals before becoming advice. Suggestions include a source and a concrete use; a release does not establish that a feature is installed or enabled.
- **Turn an idea into the next task prompt.** Select a workflow suggestion and press Enter to add a request to the coding agent's input. It asks the agent to check compatibility, propose a short workflow and verification steps, then continue work already authorized. You review and send the prompt. Skill, hook and integration setup suggestions retain their existing reviewable setup flow.
- **Bound the research.** Discovery receives only the agent name and current date, without private task details, memory or transcripts. Each session and agent gets at most one attempt per hour, one to three searches and two eligible findings, with a 45-second deadline. Failed attempts also enter the cooldown. Set `CULLY_DISCOVERY=off` to opt out; the setting travels with queued jobs to an already-running daemon. Local warnings and evidence-triggered tool-gap research remain available.

Update with `cully update --version v0.25.0`. Discovery requires working web tools in the configured agent and uses that agent's model access; it shares the automatic advisor request budget. Source states are agent-reported. See the [advisor guide](https://docs.cully.net/advisor#discover-current-techniques).

This release does not add detached server-side coding sessions, full execution replay after crashes, or automatic sandbox replacement. For service upgrades from before v0.24.0, follow the [private memory schema upgrade guide](https://docs.cully.net/memory#upgrade-the-private-schema); the v0.24.0 data migration still requires matching services and a database backup.
